hints.reason: Classic double meaning: BOXER via throwing punches, PARTY via the punch bowl; both senses are instant.

pairs.pair_note: Clean, familiar double meaning; one of the best PUNCH pairings.

hints.reason: BOXING via punches thrown, FRUIT via fruit punch the drink; both are everyday phrases.

pairs.pair_note: Solid; FRUIT side is a word join (fruit punch) but an instantly familiar one.

hints.reason: BOXING via punches, JOKE via the punchline; the comedy sense of 'punch' gives a nice click.

pairs.pair_note: Pleasing pairing; joke punchline is a well-known sense.

hints.reason: BOXING via punches, PAPER via the office hole punch; both senses are common.

pairs.pair_note: Fine, a little less fun than the party/joke versions.

hints.reason: CASINO via poker chips, COOKIE via chocolate chip cookies; strong double meaning, but the explanation and the COOKIE line ('Chocolate chip cookies.') are sentence fragments.
hints.fix: Gamblers bet with casino chips, and chocolate chips stud classic cookies.

pairs.pair_note: Strong idea; COOKIE line should also read 'Chocolate chips stud classic cookies.'

hints.reason: CASINO via betting chips, SALSA via chips and salsa; two very different senses, both instant.

pairs.pair_note: Good contrast between the two senses.

hints.reason: CHOCOLATE via chocolate lava cake, HOT via lava being molten rock; works, though HOT is a broad target and FUDGE (hot fudge) is a tighter alternative; 'about as hot as anything gets' overstates.
hints.fix: Chocolate lava cake oozes in the middle, and real lava is molten rock at well over 1,000 degrees Fahrenheit.

pairs.pair_note: Acceptable; HOT side is generic. FUDGE (hot fudge, a chocolate topping) would be a sharper hint for this pair.

hints.reason: CHOCOLATE via lava cake, LAMP via lava lamp; two familiar 'fake lava' objects, a fun click.

pairs.pair_note: Both phrases are instantly familiar and the 'neither is real lava' angle is charming.

hints.reason: CHOCOLATE via lava cake, ROCK via lava being molten rock; accurate and easy.

pairs.pair_note: Fine; ROCK side is a fact link rather than a phrase.

hints.reason: CHOCOLATE via chocolate chips, SALSA via chips and salsa; both instant.

pairs.pair_note: Solid sweet-versus-savory chip contrast.

hints.reason: CHOCOLATE via molten lava cake, VOLCANO via erupting lava; the cake is literally modeled on the volcano image.

pairs.pair_note: Excellent; the oozing-cake-as-volcano image makes it click.

hints.reason: COOKIE via chocolate chip cookies, POTATO via potato chips; easy and fair, but the explanation opens with a fragment.
hints.fix: Chocolate chips stud classic cookies, and potato chips are a classic snack.

pairs.pair_note: Good; also fix the COOKIE line fragment to 'Chocolate chips stud classic cookies.'

hints.reason: COOKIE via chocolate chip cookies, SALSA via chips and salsa; fine idea, fragment explanation.

pairs.pair_note: Good; COOKIE line needs the same fragment fix.

hints.reason: FRY lands via gulls stealing french fries, but CROW only via 'both are scavenging birds', a category link that SEAGULL does not naturally summon.

pairs.pair_note: Seagull-to-crow is just 'another bird'; would be ambiguous with any other bird on the board.

hints.reason: SNACK via gulls snatching food, CROW only via a loose 'seaside crow' scavenger comparison; the crow side is weak.

hints.reason: DRAFT via draft picks in sports, ORCHARD via apple picking; both familiar to U.S. players.

hints.reason: FISH via scales on the body, MAP via the distance scale; both senses well known.

pairs.pair_note: Fine; map scale is slightly more schoolbook than the piano or weight senses.

hints.reason: FISH via scales, PIANO via practicing scales; a classic, satisfying double meaning.

hints.reason: FISH via its scales, WEIGHT via the bathroom scale, with a bonus angler weighing a catch image.

pairs.pair_note: Strong; the 'weighing a fish on a scale' bonus reading adds charm.

hints.reason: Boardwalk scene: FRY via gulls swiping french fries, OCEAN via gulls over the sea; a vivid, shared situation.
